title: Open Subsurface Data (osd) STAC extension, v3.0.0
description: Collection fields state what our tools established about the whole record (record-level assurance, not per file or per feature). Item fields state how one feature's geometry was obtained. Enums are closed and no other osd: field is allowed. Offline validation maps this URL to schema/stac-osd.json (schema/stac/schema-map.json). v2 (E19): `osd:access` admits `purchase`; the identifier gains `?v=2`. The v1 identifier resolves to this same file online, so a document naming either identifier validates here; v1 is frozen at tests/fixtures/schema/stac-osd-1.json. v3 (E18): Items gain `osd:period_source`; the identifier gains `?v=3`; a document naming the v1 or v2 identifier validates here too; v2 is frozen at tests/fixtures/schema/stac-osd-2.json.

osd:level.description: The record's latest verification level: L0 listed; L1 origin reachable; L2 files checksummed and licence text captured; L3 outlines extracted by a reader; L4 converted with a fidelity record

osd:checked_at.description: When that level was established; null when the record was never verified

osd:access.description: As the record states it: anonymous, a free account, a documented service, a human approves, or the files are sold (v2)

osd:redistribution.description: May a third party host a copy, as the record states it

osd:blocked_since.description: Present while the origin refuses our runner: the first check of the current blocked run (OSD-D9)

osd:approximate.description: true when the geometry is a placeholder, not derived from the data

osd:derivation.description: How the geometry was derived: the outline feature's source

osd:input_sha256.description: sha256 of the input the geometry was derived from, as the outline collection's inputs state it

osd:period_source.description: Where start_datetime and end_datetime come from: feature, the feature's own start and end as the publisher's service states them (the outline's osd:period_start, osd:period_end); feature-start,collection-end, the feature's start and the Collection's end when the feature states no usable end; collection, the Collection's period (the record's) when the feature states nothing usable
